answer: Each answer stakes coin into the lagoon and is stamped with a pigment, a fingerprint of its argument. Any peer may challenge a pair whose pigment falls within a published distance of the other's; if upheld, both bonds are slashed to pay the challenger. An honest key risks one bond among strangers. A farm of N heads writes N answers from one mind, so its own pigment crowds one region and slashable pairs grow as N(N-1)/2, while the fixed pool pays each head less. Cloning becomes quadratic exposure. Each stake is cut like cedar shingles: never poolable, and slashing lands on the writer.
